text:
The headlines around David Pastrnak this week weren't about his scoring. After losses to Montreal and Minnesota he called Boston's start "UNACCEPTABLE" (Audacy), and Heavy.com framed it as winning masking a bigger problem. The Bruins have dropped three of their last four.

His own game holds up. He has 26 points in 20 games, 10 on the power play, at 3.83 points per 60, right on his track record. Nine goals on 7.7 expected is a touch hot but nothing that needs explaining, and his 73 shots lead a team that leans on him at 20:23 a night. Boston gets 54.2% of the expected goals at five on five with him out there.

Evolving-Hockey's read on last season is the context that matters: he played with teammates in the bottom 10% by impact against the 97th percentile of competition. That's the job again. Our range has him around 104 points, and his top shot speed of 95.3 mph sits in the 98th percentile. What to watch: Ty Anderson of 98.5 The Sports Hub wants Minten back on his line at five on five. Who's beside him may decide how loud Pastrnak gets next.
headline: Pastrnak is fine. He says the Bruins aren't.
